headline: Learned models infer copy number and methylation variation from sequencing data
label: Genomic Variant Detection Tools
summary: Shallow and long-read sequencing now pair with deep learning and foundation models to extract variation from cfDNA, cfRNA, and spatial data.
synthesis: The common thread across these eight publications is inference of genomic variation from sequencing-derived signals, increasingly through learned models. SPICE infers somatic CNVs and allele-specific copy number from spatial transcriptomics, and RICO estimates rDNA copy number and methylation from nanopore long reads. In cell-free settings, UNITE applies XGBoost and CNN models to bin-fragment length matrices from 0.1x shallow WGS, while GeneLLM models plasma cfRNA nucleotide sequences without gene quantification. LEAF-1 supplies fragment-level embeddings for scATAC cell typing and cfDNA cancer detection. Blended genome-exome sequencing combines low-pass WGS and deep WES in one run for imputation and CNV calling. metilene3 and PACMOS extend the toolkit to multi-condition DMR detection and projection-based multi-omic classification. The novelty lies in pairing low-cost or hybrid read designs with representations that bypass explicit gene-level or coordinate-based encoding.
